raw_model_deviations.claim_in_article: We Thought It Was AI—But There Was a Person Inside Meta’s Muse
raw_model_deviations.issue: The title turns a suggestive, subject-unspecified scenario into a claim that “we” actually thought a call was AI. The Ledger confirms some calls were made by human contract workers, but does not establish that the article’s authors or another identified group had that belief.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: The asserted first-person belief and the shift from a suggestive framing to an assertion are not established by the Ledger (changed_actor, changed_certainty, unsupported_new_claim; consequently changed_fact).
raw_model_deviations.qualifier_text: A call seemed to come from an AI agent.
same_fact_id_locations: Ring, ring. A call seemed to come from an AI agent. But as the conversation went on, the voice was not AI at all. It was a person.
Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise.
A user might think the exchange was with AI, even though a person was involved.

raw_model_deviations.claim_in_article: Meta had run a test that caused exactly this surprise.
raw_model_deviations.issue: The source describes a test that suggested or evoked this scenario, while this sentence says the test caused an actual surprise. The Ledger verifies the human-call test, not that a recipient experienced this surprise.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: It changes a scenario the test suggested into an asserted outcome caused by the test (changed_causality, changed_certainty, unsupported_new_claim; consequently changed_fact).
raw_model_deviations.qualifier_text: A call seemed to come from an AI agent.
same_fact_id_locations: We Thought It Was AI—But There Was a Person Inside Meta’s Muse
Ring, ring. A call seemed to come from an AI agent. But as the conversation went on, the voice was not AI at all. It was a person.
It was like someone took off an AI costume. Then a person stepped out.

raw_model_deviations.claim_in_article: The test began without clearly telling users that contract workers would make the calls. A user might think the exchange was with AI, even though a person was involved.
raw_model_deviations.issue: The article refers broadly to users as the people not clearly informed and potentially believing the call was AI. The Ledger describes an internal test involving Meta employees; it does not establish that users outside that test were affected.
raw_model_deviations.explanation: The affected group is broadened from the internal employee test to users generally (changed_scope; changed_actor for the affected participants; unsupported_new_claim, consequently changed_fact).
raw_model_deviations.qualifier_text: A user might think the exchange was with AI, even though a person was involved.
same_fact_id_locations: The test had begun without clearly telling users.
